title: Interleaved prefill coherence and hardware kernel adapter
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem: As tenant workloads grow and long-context sessions are common, paged attention fragmentation and small discontiguous KV allocations cause suboptimal kernel utilization and prefill stalls. Current eviction heuristics reclaim memory but often leave many narrow fragments that force wide generic kernels or trigger frequent decode pauses. This increases tail latency and unit cost.

Proposal: Implement an interleaved prefill coherence layer plus a small hardware-aware kernel adapter. The coherence layer runs opportunistic lightweight compaction sweeps during low-util periods and annotates fragment ranges with "cohesion hints" for the scheduler. The kernel adapter translates cohesion hints + runtime telemetry (sequence-length distribution, HW occupancy) into a kernel selection policy that prefers narrow, packed kernels for contiguous fragment runs and falls back to wide kernels only when fragmentation density is high.

Scope: 1) A prefill coherence worker that performs: - epochal, opportunistic micro-compaction (coalescing adjacent free fragments into co-allocable segments) - soft-quarantine for recently-evicted fragments to avoid immediate reallocation churn - generation tags to allow safe concurrent decoding without global stop-the-world compaction. 2) Kernel adapter: lightweight policy layer in the scheduler that picks from multiple kernel implementations (packed-prefill optimized, generic fused-kernel, and small-sequence specialized kernels) based on cohesion hints and current occupancy. 3) Admission controller changes: allow prefill admission to be skewed toward tenants with high-cohesion candidates to maximize reuse. 4) Metrics, experiments and canary rollout.

Goals: - Reduce average decode latency for long-context workloads by 8-15% and 95th percentile by >=10%. - Decrease per-token cost for paged workloads by 6-12% through better kernel fit. - Maintain or improve overall throughput; no regression in small-request workloads.

Constraints and trade-offs: - Compaction work consumes CPU/GPU bandwidth and interacts with autoscaling; sweeps must be low-priority and backpressure-aware. - Generation-tag approach adds metadata overhead but avoids global synchronization. - Risk of oscillation if the kernel adapter flips aggressively; requires hysteresis and cooldown windows.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmark on 3 representative paged-attention workloads shows median latency regression <= -8% and p95 <= -10% compared to baseline
Component tests for coherence worker with invariants: no memory loss, safe concurrent decodes, and idempotent compaction
Kernel adapter experiments demonstrate correct kernel selection on synthetic fragmentation patterns and do not increase small workload latency by >1%
Automated canary rollout plan with metrics (latency, token-cost, error-rate) gated and documented
Design doc and safety checklist reviewed by Runtime and Infra leads
notes: 2025-02-20: Spike implemented a prototype micro-compaction that coalesces adjacent free fragments; observed 4% median latency win on ToyChat workload.
2025-02-24: Runtime lead (Asha Patel) suggested generation tags rather than global locks to allow compaction during decode - accepted.
2025-02-27: Design review: agreed to limit compaction CPU budget and expose a runtime flag for canary. Action: add backpressure metrics and a compaction budgeter (ENG-855322).
2025-03-02: Initial kernel adapter simulation shows correct selection in 93% of sampled traces. Need hysteresis to avoid thrash between packed and generic kernels.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike): prototype coherence worker + simulation (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (MVP): safe micro-compaction + kernel adapter in simulator; unit tests (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (Canary): deploy to limited tenants with runtime flag and metrics (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (Rollout): tuned budgeter, full rollout in runtime-1.19 (1 week)
rollback_plan: Disable runtime flag to revert to baseline scheduler
Drain in-flight compaction jobs and abort new compactions
Immediate kernel adapter fallback to baseline kernel selection
